newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends soft on month-end dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends soft on month-end dollar demand.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed slightly weaker but stable on Wednesday after a quiet session due to dollar short-covering ahead of the end of the month, traders said.
"Volume thinned almost to a standstill towards the close, but dealers covered some month-end (dollar) shorts," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 0.75 and 0.5 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.9050/7.9075 and 7.9000/7.9030 per dollar.
Dealers said peso weakness had been checked by a stable U.S. long bond and higher domestic primary rates.
"The market was very quiet, almost dead. What greatly helped stability was was the Cetes rate hike, which the market welcomed, and less pressure on the (U.S.) long bond," another trader said.
Banco de Mexico placed bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at 18.31 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, a hike of 24 basis points since last week.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were unchanged at a yield of 7.03 percent in late trade.
Same-day peso contracts had closed earlier two centavos firmer at 7.8990/7.9020 per dollar after lagging behind the market.
